protocol: Repeated simulated exposures at 35000 and 40000 ft. The number of chamber flights and the exposure history by person are unknown.
outcome_window: Both hips were radiographed. The interval since last exposure and later follow-up are unreported.
locator: Allen et al. 1974 p. 17 (PDF p. 33), Ratnoff paragraph
note: No changes matching the caisson-worker pattern were described in the 21 people. Two had equivocal findings, and neither of those two reported a history of bends. Acute DCS status is unreported across the sample.

protocol: One B-29 crew member reported two symptomatic cabin decompressions in one week, at 35000 and 45000 ft. The source reports at least one hour at altitude on each occasion.
outcome_window: Acute symptoms lasted several days. Hip symptoms persisted after the second episode. The clinical report documents diagnosis by 1962 and a prosthetic femoral head in 1965.
locator: Hodgson et al. 1968 p. 420, retrospective hospital case and Figure 4
note: A selected aircraft case from the hospital files. Count one affected person with two reported bends episodes. The original operator cohort does not supply a denominator for this case. The 1974 workshop reprises this case.

protocol: The pilot was working as an aerial camera operator during the approximately 1955 index exposure in an unpressurized aircraft. He reported further episodes on later flights.
outcome_window: Index pain persisted for four days after landing. Left humeral head damage was identified in May 1967, with fragment separation documented on repeat radiographs six weeks later.
locator: Fryer 1969 p. 278 (PDF p. 272), Case 28 and Figures 13-1 and 13-2
note: One selected person with repeatedly reported symptoms. The source describes no prior diving or compressed air exposure. Clinical adjudication and timeline are as reported. The 1974 workshop reprises this case.
